title: Host capacity: machine-wide admission of expensive operations

Observers.description: How each platform reads the memory a process tree holds. The measure is the footprint: what the processes hold privately plus what was swapped or compressed out of them (macOS phys_footprint, Linux proportional set size plus swapped proportional set size, Windows private commit of the process (K32GetProcessMemoryInfo PrivateUsage)). The resident set stays at the high-water mark of a process after it freed memory on macOS and does not count compressed pages at all, so it is the fallback of a platform whose footprint source cannot be read, never the first choice. The store of learned peaks is stamped with the measure, so peaks of another measure never mix with it.

rampIdleAfterMilliseconds.description: A grant that held its ramp slot this long without using the memory it reserved (below rampIdleObservedBasisPoints of it) stops counting toward maximumRamping: it is idle at an inner gate, not growing. Its unrealized reservation still counts as committed memory.

rampIdleKeepMegabytes.description: With rampIdleKeepBasisPoints: what an idle ramping grant (see rampIdleAfterMilliseconds) is still charged beside what it holds, so the unused rest of its reservation is released to others.

settledAfterMilliseconds.description: With settledKeepBasisPoints: how long a grant has run since it was admitted or resumed before its measurement replaces its estimate. A settled grant is charged settledKeepBasisPoints of what it measurably holds (never under rampIdleKeepMegabytes, never more than it reserved).

interactiveReserveBasisPoints.description: With the minimum and maximum: the memory kept for the interactive apps of the host (editor, assistant and its helpers, terminal), a share of its memory between the bounds; admission treats at least this much as taken by what is not granted, however little those apps hold right now.

sessionCapBasisPoints.description: The most memory one agent session may hold charged at once (the reservation of a ramping grant, what a grown grant measurably holds), a share of the host memory: a further request of a session that already holds reservations waits (reason session-cap) while the reservations plus its least need would pass it and another agent session has a request waiting that could itself be served under the cap; work-conserving: sessions whose competitors only hold grants, or that are alone on the host, are judged by memory alone.

childStartMegabytes.description: What a farm child (a grant of a run's worker) is charged per job while it boots or idles, or what it measurably holds when that is more: its memory sits inside the tree of the run and is already out of the available memory.

ceilingBasisPoints.description: Occupied swap above this share of the host memory is crowded. Occupancy alone never stops admission: a host that has run for days keeps cold pages in swap.

activeBasisPointsPerSecond.description: Swap traffic (pages swapped in plus out) per second, as a share of the host memory in basis points, from which swap counts as worked. 0.6 is 1 MB/s on a 16 GB host.

outBasisPointsPerSecond.description: Swap traffic per second, as a share of the host memory in basis points, above which the host waits whatever its free memory is. 40 is 64 MB/s on a 16 GB host.

shortBasisPoints.description: Crowded and worked swap only stops admission while the memory the host can still give out is below this share of its memory: swap traffic with plenty of reclaimable memory is the host tidying up, not a shortage.

deadlineInteractiveMilliseconds.description: How long an interactive request waits for memory before a soft stop may admit a shrinkable minimum that fits. A hard stop continues to hold admission while the wait names the blockers.

deadlineBatchMilliseconds.description: The same deadline for a batch request, which may wait longer than an interactive one.

starvedMilliseconds.description: How long a request can wait without a fitting reservation or while a hard stop holds before it is refused as starved.

pressure.description: Worst of native pressure, memory availability within the physical or cgroup boundary, and compressor occupancy relative to physical memory. A declared scheduling profile changes the available budget without rescaling physical pressure.

compressedMegabytes.description: The megabytes the memory compressor occupies (macOS: pages occupied by the compressor); absent where the platform does not report it.

unmanagedMegabytes.description: The memory held by everything the gate did not grant (agent CLIs, editors, watchers, tool daemons): what the machine uses beyond the free memory minus what its grants observe. The budget of the gate is what is left of the machine after it.

priority.description: The class of a request. `interactive` is served before `batch`; `lent` is work of another machine of the fleet running here: it is served after every request of this machine, never ages into a higher class, and is admitted only while no request of this machine waits, so a lent action takes only capacity the local user is not asking for.

essential.description: The first elastic worker may start despite a shortage of free memory or a soft stop. Hard stops for critical pressure or active swap hold all workers.

en.waiting: [capacity] waiting {seconds}s for {operation}: {reason} (need {need} MB; {spare} MB spare = {available} MB available - {floor} MB floor - {held} MB reserved but not yet resident - {taken} MB admitted ahead{short}; load {load}; {running} running, {ahead} ahead); behind {behind}
en.admitted: [capacity] admitted {operation}: {jobs} job(s), {reserved} MB reserved ({available} MB available, {floor} MB floor)
en.reduced: [capacity] admitted {operation} with {jobs} of {preferred} job(s): the host cannot carry more right now
en.override: [capacity] admitted {operation} after {seconds}s although {reason}: nothing of ours is running and memory holds
en.unsatisfiable: [capacity] admitted {operation} after {seconds}s with {reserved} MB of the {asked} MB it asked for: even if every run of ours ended the host would have only {available} MB above its {floor} MB floor, so waiting can never free more
en.bypassed: [capacity] host capacity governor is switched off ({switch}=off)
en.status: [capacity] {available} MB available of {total} MB (floor {floor} MB, {spare} MB spare), pressure {pressure}, swap {swap} MB, load {load}, open files {files}, attached images {images}; {grants} running, {waiters} waiting
en.grant: [capacity]   running {id} {operation}: {jobs} job(s), {reserved} MB reserved, {observed} MB observed, pid {pid}, since {seconds}s

reasons.swap: swap is crowded and worked while memory is short
reasons.swap-activity: the host is swapping out too fast
reasons.files: the machine has too many open files
reasons.attaches: too many disk images are attached
reasons.load: the cores are fully booked by our own running jobs
reasons.queue-order: an earlier request is still waiting
reasons.session-cap: this agent session already holds its share of the memory reservations
reasons.ramp: too many learned reservations are still growing to their peak
reasons.quiet-limit: enough quiet reservations are already held
reasons.never: the request can never fit this machine
reasons.starved: not even the least memory it needs is free and nothing of ours is running

errors.grantIdentifierRequired: Closed inherited host capacity grant identifier required
errors.floorOrder: Host capacity floor minimum exceeds its maximum
errors.pressureOrder: Host capacity pressure thresholds must rise from warn to critical
errors.planJobs: Host capacity plan needs jobs between the request bounds
errors.inheritedIdentifier: Closed inherited host capacity grant identifier required
errors.quietUpgradeRequired: a quiet request needs the full request it may grow into, under the same id
errors.exactGrantRequired: An explicit capacity command requires a live reservation of at least {minimum} MB and {cores} core(s); the current grant supplies {reserved} MB and {availablecores} core(s). Run it outside the enclosing grant or enable capacity admission.
errors.memoryNeverFits: {operation} needs at least {minimum} MB of memory, but this machine has {total} MB of which {floor} MB stay reserved, so at most {capacity} MB can ever be given out. It cannot run here: use a machine with more memory (at least {needed} MB), or take the result from the fleet cache instead of computing it here.
errors.memoryStarved: {operation} needs at least {minimum} MB of free memory, but after {seconds} s only {spare} MB are free above the {floor} MB floor of this machine ({total} MB) and nothing of ours is running, so waiting longer cannot help. Close other applications (or stop the resident graph service with `repo service host stop`, which can hold more than 1 GB) until {minimum} MB are free, then run the command again.
errors.memoryWaitedOut: {operation} needs at least {minimum} MB of free memory, but after {seconds} s only {spare} MB are free above the {floor} MB floor of this machine ({total} MB); it is held by {holders}. The wait ends here instead of going on for ever: run the command again once those finish, or stop them.

en.handover: [capacity] keeping the {operation} grant ({jobs} job(s), {reserved} MB reserved) for the command that replaces this one: it does not queue again
en.adopted: [capacity] took over the {operation} grant of the command this one replaces ({jobs} job(s), {reserved} MB reserved): no queue
en.handoverRefused: [capacity] the grant of the command this one replaces cannot be taken over ({reason}): queueing like any other request

handoverReasons.gone: the grant is gone or no longer current
handoverReasons.token: the handover token does not match
handoverReasons.identity: this process is not the one the grant was offered to
handoverReasons.operation: it was granted for another operation

en.estimated: [capacity] {operation}: sized at {percent}% of the default from {samples} earlier run(s) of its class
en.treeUnobserved: [capacity] the memory of running process trees cannot be observed on {platform} ({reason}); nothing is learned from this run and admission uses the declared sizes
en.footprintFallback: [capacity] the memory footprint of running process trees cannot be read on {platform} ({reason}); the resident set is used instead, which can overstate what a process holds
en.countersPartial: [capacity] the {platform} memory counters could not be read ({reason}); pressure and swap are unknown (unknown is not pressure), available memory is the operating system's free memory
en.availableUnread: [capacity] the memory this {platform} host can still give out cannot be read ({reason}); limits that depend on it are not applied and no run waits for it
en.phased: [capacity] {operation}: sized at {percent}% of the default from {samples} earlier run(s) of its class, at least {floor} MB because of its {phase} phase
en.quiet: [capacity] {operation}: forecast quiet because the last run of its class executed nothing ({samples} quiet run(s) behind its size, {percent}% of the recent runs): {reserved} MB reserved now, the full {full} MB only if work has to run
en.upgrading: [capacity] {operation}: work has to run, waiting {seconds}s to grow the reservation from {from} MB to {to} MB: {reason} ({spare} MB spare above the {floor} MB floor; {running} running, {ahead} ahead); behind {behind}
en.upgraded: [capacity] {operation}: reservation grown from {from} MB to {to} MB after {seconds}s ({jobs} job(s), {available} MB available, {floor} MB floor)
en.upgradedPartly: [capacity] {operation}: reservation grown from {from} MB to {to} MB of the {wanted} MB it asked for, after {seconds}s: nothing else of ours is running (other runs of ours only wait to grow) and only that much memory is free ({available} MB available, {floor} MB floor); the run goes on with {jobs} of {preferred} job(s)
en.upgradedReduced: [capacity] {operation}: reservation grown from {from} MB to {to} MB with {jobs} of {preferred} job(s) after {seconds}s: the host cannot carry more right now ({available} MB available, {floor} MB floor); the run grows to more jobs once memory and cores free up
en.upgradeWithdrawn: [capacity] {operation}: the request to grow the reservation was withdrawn after {seconds}s; the run keeps its {reserved} MB
en.grantQuiet: [capacity]   quiet {id} {operation}: forecast to execute nothing, {reserved} MB reserved instead of its full request, {observed} MB observed, pid {pid}, since {seconds}s
en.waiterUpgrade: [capacity]   growing {id} {operation}: wants {jobs} job(s), {need} MB, since {seconds}s, pid {pid}
en.quietFollowUp: [capacity] {operation}: forecast quiet because the earlier run of its class finished {seconds}s ago and left its results cached: {reserved} MB reserved now, the full {full} MB only if work has to run
en.reducedGrows: [capacity] admitted {operation} with {jobs} of {preferred} job(s): the host cannot carry more right now; the run grows to more jobs once memory frees up
en.grown: [capacity] {operation}: grown from {from} to {jobs} of {preferred} job(s) after {seconds}s, reservation {before} MB -> {reserved} MB: memory freed up and nothing of ours waits ({available} MB available, {floor} MB floor); work that starts from now on uses the new jobs
en.shrunk: [capacity] admitted {operation} with {reserved} of {wanted} MB: only {spare} MB are free above the {floor} MB floor right now, and {minimum} MB are enough to start
en.shrunkStopped: [capacity] admitted {operation} with {reserved} of {wanted} MB after waiting {seconds}s (limit {limit}s): {reason}, but {spare} MB are free above the {floor} MB floor and {minimum} MB are enough to start
en.blockerSelf: this very run ({megabytes} MB, its own grant)
en.lent: [capacity] admitted {operation} inside the reservation of {holder}: {jobs} job(s), {reserved} MB lent from its unused part, the parent keeps what it needs

de.waiting: [capacity] wartet seit {seconds} s auf {operation}: {reason} (benötigt {need} MB; {spare} MB frei = {available} MB verfügbar - {floor} MB Untergrenze - {held} MB reserviert, aber noch nicht belegt - {taken} MB davor zugelassen{short}; Last {load}; {running} laufen, {ahead} davor); hinter {behind}
de.admitted: [capacity] zugelassen {operation}: {jobs} Job(s), {reserved} MB reserviert ({available} MB verfügbar, Untergrenze {floor} MB)
de.reduced: [capacity] {operation} mit {jobs} von {preferred} Job(s) zugelassen: der Rechner trägt gerade nicht mehr
de.override: [capacity] {operation} nach {seconds} s zugelassen, obwohl {reason}: nichts von uns läuft und der Speicher reicht
de.unsatisfiable: [capacity] {operation} nach {seconds} s mit {reserved} MB der angefragten {asked} MB zugelassen: selbst wenn jeder Lauf von uns endete, hätte der Rechner nur {available} MB über seiner Reserve von {floor} MB, Warten kann also nie mehr freigeben
de.status: [capacity] {available} MB verfügbar von {total} MB (Untergrenze {floor} MB, {spare} MB frei), Speicherdruck {pressure}, Auslagerung {swap} MB, Last {load}, offene Dateien {files}, eingehängte Images {images}; {grants} laufen, {waiters} warten
de.grant: [capacity]   läuft {id} {operation}: {jobs} Job(s), {reserved} MB reserviert, {observed} MB beobachtet, pid {pid}, seit {seconds} s
de.waiter: [capacity]   wartet {id} {operation}: möchte {jobs} Job(s), {need} MB, seit {seconds} s, pid {pid}
de.grantLent: [capacity]   verliehen {id} {operation}: sein Prozess wartet nur in einer Schlange, darum zählen die {reserved} MB reserviert und {cpu} Kern(e) für niemanden ({observed} MB beobachtet, pid {pid}, seit {seconds} s)

reasons.swap: die Auslagerung ist voll und wird bewegt, während der Speicher knapp ist
reasons.swap-activity: der Rechner lagert zu schnell aus
reasons.files: der Rechner hat zu viele offene Dateien
reasons.load: die Kerne sind von unseren laufenden Jobs voll belegt
reasons.session-cap: diese Agentensitzung hält schon ihren Anteil an Speicherreservierungen
reasons.ramp: zu viele gelernte Reservierungen wachsen noch auf ihren Spitzenwert an
reasons.quiet-limit: es werden schon genug ruhige Reservierungen gehalten
reasons.never: die Anfrage passt nie auf diesen Rechner
reasons.starved: nicht einmal der kleinste benötigte Speicher ist frei, und nichts von uns läuft

errors.grantIdentifierRequired: Geschlossene Kennung der geerbten Kapazitätszusage des Rechners erforderlich
errors.queueFull: Die Warteschlange der Rechnerkapazität ist voll
errors.floorOrder: Die Untergrenze der Rechnerkapazität überschreitet ihre Obergrenze
errors.pressureOrder: Die Schwellen des Speicherdrucks müssen von Warnung zu kritisch steigen
errors.planJobs: Der Kapazitätsplan braucht Jobs zwischen den Grenzen der Anfrage
errors.inheritedIdentifier: Eine gültige Kennung der geerbten Rechner-Kapazitätszusage ist erforderlich
errors.quietUpgradeRequired: eine ruhige Anfrage braucht die volle Anfrage, in die sie wachsen darf, unter derselben Kennung
errors.exactGrantRequired: Ein Befehl mit expliziter Kapazitätsangabe benötigt eine aktive Reservierung von mindestens {minimum} MB und {cores} Kern(en). Die aktuelle Zusage stellt {reserved} MB und {availablecores} Kern(e) bereit. Den Befehl außerhalb der umgebenden Zusage ausführen oder die Kapazitätszulassung aktivieren.
errors.memoryNeverFits: {operation} braucht mindestens {minimum} MB Speicher, dieser Rechner hat aber {total} MB, von denen {floor} MB reserviert bleiben, also können höchstens {capacity} MB vergeben werden. Es kann hier nicht laufen: einen Rechner mit mehr Speicher verwenden (mindestens {needed} MB) oder das Ergebnis aus dem Flottencache holen, statt es hier zu berechnen.
errors.memoryStarved: {operation} braucht mindestens {minimum} MB freien Speicher, aber nach {seconds} s sind nur {spare} MB über der Untergrenze von {floor} MB dieses Rechners ({total} MB) frei, und nichts von uns läuft; längeres Warten hilft nicht. Andere Anwendungen schließen (oder den residenten Graphdienst mit `repo service host stop` beenden, er kann über 1 GB halten), bis {minimum} MB frei sind, und den Befehl dann erneut ausführen.
errors.memoryWaitedOut: {operation} braucht mindestens {minimum} MB freien Speicher, aber nach {seconds} s sind nur {spare} MB über der Untergrenze von {floor} MB dieses Rechners ({total} MB) frei; belegt von {holders}. Das Warten endet hier, statt ewig weiterzugehen: den Befehl erneut ausführen, sobald diese fertig sind, oder sie beenden.

de.handover: [capacity] die Zusage für {operation} ({jobs} Job(s), {reserved} MB reserviert) bleibt für den Befehl, der diesen ersetzt: er reiht sich nicht erneut ein
de.adopted: [capacity] Zusage für {operation} des ersetzten Befehls übernommen ({jobs} Job(s), {reserved} MB reserviert): keine Warteschlange
de.handoverRefused: [capacity] die Zusage des ersetzten Befehls kann nicht übernommen werden ({reason}): Anfrage reiht sich wie jede andere ein

handoverReasons.gone: die Zusage ist erloschen oder nicht mehr aktuell
handoverReasons.identity: dieser Prozess ist nicht der, dem die Zusage angeboten wurde
handoverReasons.operation: sie wurde für eine andere Operation erteilt

de.estimated: [capacity] {operation}: auf {percent} % des Standardwerts bemessen, aus {samples} früheren Läufen seiner Klasse
de.treeUnobserved: [capacity] Der Speicher laufender Prozessbäume kann unter {platform} nicht beobachtet werden ({reason}); aus diesem Lauf wird nichts gelernt und die Zulassung nutzt die deklarierten Größen
de.footprintFallback: [capacity] Der Speicher-Fußabdruck laufender Prozessbäume kann unter {platform} nicht gelesen werden ({reason}); stattdessen gilt der residente Speicher, der überschätzen kann, was ein Prozess hält
de.countersPartial: [capacity] Die Speicherzähler von {platform} konnten nicht gelesen werden ({reason}); Speicherdruck und Auslagerung sind unbekannt (unbekannt ist kein Druck), verfügbar ist der freie Speicher des Betriebssystems
de.availableUnread: [capacity] der Speicher, den dieser {platform}-Host noch hergeben kann, ist nicht lesbar ({reason}); davon abhängige Grenzen gelten nicht und kein Lauf wartet darauf
de.phased: [capacity] {operation}: auf {percent} % des Standardwerts bemessen, aus {samples} früheren Läufen seiner Klasse, mindestens {floor} MB wegen der Phase {phase}
de.quiet: [capacity] {operation}: ruhig prognostiziert, weil der letzte Lauf seiner Klasse nichts ausführte ({samples} ruhige Läufe hinter ihrer Größe, {percent} % der jüngsten Läufe): jetzt {reserved} MB reserviert, die vollen {full} MB nur, wenn Arbeit laufen muss
de.upgrading: [capacity] {operation}: es muss Arbeit laufen, wartet seit {seconds} s darauf, die Reservierung von {from} MB auf {to} MB zu vergrößern: {reason} ({spare} MB frei oberhalb der Untergrenze von {floor} MB; {running} laufen, {ahead} davor); hinter {behind}
de.upgraded: [capacity] {operation}: Reservierung nach {seconds} s von {from} MB auf {to} MB vergrößert ({jobs} Job(s), {available} MB verfügbar, Untergrenze {floor} MB)
de.upgradedPartly: [capacity] {operation}: Reservierung nach {seconds} s von {from} MB auf {to} MB der angefragten {wanted} MB vergrößert: nichts anderes von uns läuft (andere Läufe von uns warten nur auf ihr Wachstum) und mehr Speicher ist nicht frei ({available} MB verfügbar, Untergrenze {floor} MB); der Lauf geht mit {jobs} von {preferred} Job(s) weiter
de.upgradedReduced: [capacity] {operation}: Reservierung nach {seconds} s von {from} MB auf {to} MB mit {jobs} von {preferred} Job(s) vergrößert: der Rechner trägt gerade nicht mehr ({available} MB verfügbar, Untergrenze {floor} MB); der Lauf wächst auf mehr Jobs, sobald Speicher und Kerne frei werden
de.upgradeWithdrawn: [capacity] {operation}: die Anfrage, die Reservierung zu vergrößern, wurde nach {seconds} s zurückgezogen; der Lauf behält seine {reserved} MB
de.grantQuiet: [capacity]   ruhig {id} {operation}: soll nichts ausführen, {reserved} MB statt der vollen Anfrage reserviert, {observed} MB beobachtet, pid {pid}, seit {seconds} s
de.waiterUpgrade: [capacity]   wächst {id} {operation}: möchte {jobs} Job(s), {need} MB, seit {seconds} s, pid {pid}
de.quietFollowUp: [capacity] {operation}: ruhig prognostiziert, weil der frühere Lauf seiner Klasse vor {seconds} s endete und seine Ergebnisse zwischengespeichert hinterließ: jetzt {reserved} MB reserviert, die vollen {full} MB nur, wenn Arbeit laufen muss
de.reducedGrows: [capacity] {operation} mit {jobs} von {preferred} Job(s) zugelassen: der Rechner trägt gerade nicht mehr; der Lauf wächst auf mehr Jobs, sobald Speicher frei wird
de.grown: [capacity] {operation}: nach {seconds} s von {from} auf {jobs} von {preferred} Job(s) gewachsen, Reservierung {before} MB -> {reserved} MB: Speicher ist frei geworden und nichts von uns wartet ({available} MB verfügbar, Untergrenze {floor} MB); Arbeit, die ab jetzt startet, nutzt die neuen Jobs
de.shrunk: [capacity] {operation} mit {reserved} von {wanted} MB zugelassen: gerade sind nur {spare} MB über der Untergrenze von {floor} MB frei, und {minimum} MB genügen zum Start
de.shrunkStopped: [capacity] {operation} mit {reserved} von {wanted} MB nach {seconds}s Wartezeit (Grenze {limit}s) zugelassen: {reason}, aber {spare} MB über der Untergrenze von {floor} MB sind frei und {minimum} MB genügen zum Start
de.blockerSelf: dieser Lauf selbst ({megabytes} MB, seine eigene Zusage)
de.lent: [capacity] {operation} innerhalb der Reservierung von {holder} zugelassen: {jobs} Job(s), {reserved} MB aus dem ungenutzten Teil geliehen, der Elternprozess behält, was er braucht

maximumPhaseMegabytes.description: The most the learned size of the assembly or plan phase may be: both phases only prepare the run and read a served graph, so a peak above this (a thrashing host counts shared and compressed pages many times) is no evidence of what they need and never sets a reservation. The graph build (rebuild) has its own bounds.

rebuildMinimumMegabytes.description: The least a graph rebuild runs with: its farm at width one. A rebuild booking is shrinkable down to this and never refused for memory above it.

rebuildQuantileBasisPoints.description: The quantile of the recent rebuild readings a learned rebuild size follows (the median by default), so one cold run cannot pin later requests.

Envelope.description: 🧰️ The resources a target holds at its peak when it runs several workers of its own (end-to-end suites): any target whose name matches `pattern` is sized at least at `cpu` cores and `megabytes` per job, whatever kind the worker pool classifies it as.

Ceiling.description: The most a class of runs may ever ask for, whatever its learned ratio says: a declared bound on the class key (`operation:kind:project:target`) that holds until the class has measured enough runs to be capped by its own peaks.

Limits.description: EN: The probe, heartbeat and cache limits of the host capacity engine. DE: Die Probe-, Herzschlag- und Cache-Grenzen der Host-Kapazitaets-Engine.

en.optionalProbeMilliseconds: How long an optional counter probe (disk images, memory pressure) may run before it is abandoned.
en.commandTimeoutMilliseconds: The hard timeout of one platform command that reads a counter.
en.commandOutputBytes: The most output bytes of one platform command that is read (4 MiB).
en.defaultPageBytes: The memory page size assumed when the platform does not report one.
en.reasonCharacters: The most characters of the reason a failed probe reports.
en.heartbeatFirstMilliseconds: The longest wait before the first heartbeat of a waiting request, whatever the policy interval says.
en.settledOutcomeLimit: The most upgrade outcomes remembered by key; the oldest goes first.
en.quickQuantileBasisPoints: The quantile of the active time, in basis points, that decides whether a class of runs counts as quick (the median).
en.availableAgeMilliseconds: How long one reading of the memory the host can still give out is reused before the platform is asked again.
en.availableCommandMilliseconds: The hard timeout of the command (macOS: vm_stat) that reads the memory the host can still give out.

de.optionalProbeMilliseconds: Wie lange eine optionale Zaehlerabfrage (Disk-Images, Speicherdruck) laufen darf, bevor sie verworfen wird.
de.commandTimeoutMilliseconds: Das harte Zeitlimit eines Plattformbefehls, der einen Zähler liest.
de.commandOutputBytes: Die meisten Ausgabebytes eines Plattformbefehls, die gelesen werden (4 MiB).
de.defaultPageBytes: Die angenommene Speicherseitengroesse, wenn die Plattform keine meldet.
de.reasonCharacters: Die meisten Zeichen des Grundes, den eine fehlgeschlagene Abfrage meldet.
de.heartbeatFirstMilliseconds: Die längste Wartezeit bis zum ersten Herzschlag einer wartenden Anfrage, egal was das Richtlinien-Intervall sagt.
de.settledOutcomeLimit: Die meisten nach Schlüssel gemerkten Hochstufungs-Ergebnisse; das älteste geht zuerst.
de.quickQuantileBasisPoints: Das Quantil der aktiven Zeit in Basispunkten, das entscheidet, ob eine Laufklasse als schnell gilt (der Median).
de.availableAgeMilliseconds: Wie lange eine Messung des Speichers, den der Host noch hergeben kann, wiederverwendet wird, bevor die Plattform erneut gefragt wird.
de.availableCommandMilliseconds: Das harte Zeitlimit des Befehls (macOS: vm_stat), der den Speicher liest, den der Host noch hergeben kann.

Unmanaged.description: The classes the unmanaged processes of a host census are counted in, first match wins; `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,rss=,comm=` names them on Linux and macOS.
